exam.q: General appearance and work of breathing
exam.a: Alert and active; no respiratory distress; no chest-wall retraction.

exam.q: Inspection of the lip and nose
exam.a: Unilateral left-sided cleft lip involving the vermilion and extending minimally into the nostril sill; left alar base mildly flattened compared with the right.

exam.q: Oral cavity: hard and soft palate
exam.a: Hard and soft palate intact and continuous; no overt cleft palate, no notch at the posterior hard palate, no bifid uvula.

exam.q: Observation of suck and feeding during examination
exam.a: Near-complete lip seal around the nipple/teat with minor air leak at the left oral commissure; rhythmic suck–swallow coordination; no nasal regurgitation.
Moist mucous membranes; capillary refill time normal; weight loss within the expected physiological range for a neonate.
No significant murmur; good peripheral perfusion.
Both auricles structurally normal; no visible anomaly.
No syndactyly, polydactyly or other craniofacial anomaly on screening examination.

exam.q: Airway assessment in the supine position
exam.a: No stertor and no oxygen desaturation when supine (key pertinent negative distinguishing this from Pierre Robin sequence).

problemList: Congenital unilateral cleft lip without cleft palate on initial examination
Near-normal feeding with minor milk leakage at the oral commissure; no nasal regurgitation
Weight loss within the physiological neonatal range; requires ongoing growth monitoring
Incomplete screening for associated anomalies and hearing
Significant parental aesthetic and psychosocial distress requiring support
G1C1.problemRepresentation: A 5-day-old female neonate with a congenital isolated unilateral cleft lip, without cleft palate or airway/feeding red flags on initial examination, with adequate feeding and physiological weight loss but high parental aesthetic distress, requiring exclusion of occult associated anomalies, feeding/growth surveillance, and referral to the multidisciplinary cleft team for age-appropriate surgical planning.

exam.q: General appearance and work of breathing
exam.a: Alert and active; no respiratory distress in any position.

exam.q: Inspection of the oral cavity and palate
exam.a: Complete cleft of the soft and hard palate; no associated cleft lip.
Normal mandibular size; no micrognathia (critical in distinguishing this from Pierre Robin sequence).
Normal tongue position; no glossoptosis.

exam.q: Positional airway observation (supine vs prone vs upright)
exam.a: No stertor, desaturation or retraction in any tested position (key pertinent negative distinguishing this from Pierre Robin sequence, Card 6).

exam.q: Feeding observation with a specialized cleft feeder
exam.a: Mild nasal regurgitation of milk during sucking, with preserved rhythmic swallowing.
Moist mucous membranes; weight gain below the expected trajectory but not yet critical.
Both tympanic membranes mildly dull, suggestive of early bilateral middle-ear effusion; no otalgia or fever.
No syndactyly, craniofacial anomaly or other limb anomaly.
No significant murmur; good peripheral perfusion.

problemList: Isolated complete cleft of the soft and hard palate without micrognathia or glossoptosis
Feeding inefficiency with nasal regurgitation, without positional airway compromise
Suboptimal weight gain requiring monitoring and modification of feeding technique
Suspected early bilateral middle-ear effusion requiring audiological confirmation
Not yet enrolled in a multidisciplinary cleft pathway for speech, hearing and surgical planning
G1C2.problemRepresentation: A 3-week-old male infant with an isolated complete cleft palate, without micrognathia or glossoptosis and with a normal positional airway assessment, presenting with feeding inefficiency, nasal regurgitation, suboptimal weight gain and suspected early middle-ear effusion, requiring feeding optimization, audiological/ENT evaluation to protect speech-language development, and multidisciplinary cleft team referral, with no current indication of an airway emergency.

exam.q: Inspection of both hands and feet
exam.a: Complete cutaneous syndactyly of the left ring and little fingers extending from the web space to near the nail fold; right hand and both feet normal.
Two separate nail plates; no synonychia.
Mild length discrepancy between the ring and little fingers, suggestive of a developing tethering effect with growth.

exam.q: Active and passive range of motion
exam.a: Mild flexion deformity and lateral deviation of the distal digits on full extension due to tethering; near-full flexion preserved.
Capillary refill and sensation grossly intact in both digits.
No palpable abnormal bony prominence; radiographs still required to exclude osseous involvement.

exam.q: Functional task observation (pencil grip, simulated scissor use)
exam.a: Slow task performance with a compensatory grip due to restricted independent digit abduction.

exam.q: Screening for syndromic features (craniofacial, other digits, cardiac)
exam.a: No craniofacial anomaly, polydactyly or other limb anomaly on screening examination (pertinent negative).

problemList: Congenital complete cutaneous syndactyly of the left ring and little fingers
Mild growth-related tethering deformity due to digit length discrepancy
Functional impairment of fine-motor tasks affecting school performance
Simple versus complex (osseous) syndactyly not yet differentiated radiographically
No syndromic features on screening examination; comprehensive evaluation incomplete
G1C3.problemRepresentation: A 6-year-old boy with congenital complete cutaneous syndactyly of the left ring and little fingers, complicated by mild growth-related tethering deformity and progressive fine-motor functional impairment, without syndromic features on screening examination, requiring radiographic differentiation of simple versus complex syndactyly, assessment of functional and growth implications, and referral to hand/plastic surgery for age-appropriate management planning.

exam.q: Head shape (vertex, frontal and lateral views)
exam.a: Turribrachycephalic pattern with bilateral frontal bossing; symmetric but progressively abnormal contour, not the asymmetric occipital flattening of positional plagiocephaly.
Palpable ridging along both coronal sutures.
Anterior fontanelle closing earlier than expected for age.
Occipitofrontal circumference crossing percentiles upward over the last two visits.
Grossly age-appropriate on screening assessment (key pertinent negative).

exam.q: Eye examination (proptosis, sunset sign, red reflex)
exam.a: No proptosis or sunsetting on this examination; formal ophthalmological assessment not yet performed.
Alert and interactive; no lethargy or high-pitched cry.
No overt syndromic features on screening examination.

problemList: Progressive cranial deformity since 2 months of age, unresponsive to repositioning
Bilateral palpable coronal suture ridging with premature anterior fontanelle closure
Abnormal head circumference trajectory crossing percentiles
No overt signs of raised intracranial pressure or visual compromise; formal assessment pending
No syndromic features on screening examination
G1C4.problemRepresentation: A 5-month-old female infant with progressive cranial deformity since 2 months of age unresponsive to repositioning, with bilateral palpable coronal suture ridging, premature anterior fontanelle closure and an abnormal head circumference trajectory, without overt signs of raised intracranial pressure or visual compromise, most consistent with craniosynostosis rather than positional plagiocephaly, requiring prompt craniofacial/neurosurgical referral for diagnostic confirmation and systematic ICP and visual assessment.

exam.q: Inspection of the right external ear
exam.a: Grade III microtia: severely hypoplastic, malformed auricle with rudimentary remnants only.
Suspected external auditory canal atresia (no visible patent canal); requires specialist confirmation.
Auricle and canal grossly normal on examination (pertinent negative; audiological confirmation still required as true hearing thresholds are unknown).
Suspected mild right mandibular hypoplasia with subtle facial asymmetry; requires further evaluation.
Clearly better orienting response to sound presented on the left than on the right.

exam.q: Screening of speech and language interaction
exam.a: Expressive vocabulary below the expected level for a 3-year-old.
No observable facial nerve weakness.
No overt vertebral, cardiac or limb anomaly on screening examination.

problemList: Right grade III microtia with suspected external auditory canal atresia
Lost to follow-up after newborn hearing screening; bilateral hearing status unconfirmed
Expressive speech-language delay for age
Suspected mild right mandibular hypoplasia and facial asymmetry requiring evaluation
Psychosocial concerns for the child and family related to appearance and teasing
G1C5.problemRepresentation: A 3-year-old boy with right grade III microtia and suspected external auditory canal atresia, lost to follow-up after newborn hearing screening, now presenting with expressive speech-language delay and suspected mild right mandibular hypoplasia, requiring urgent formal bilateral audiological assessment, multidisciplinary ENT/craniofacial referral for hearing rehabilitation and staged reconstruction planning, and developmental and psychosocial support.

exam.q: General appearance, work of breathing and airway
exam.a: Alert but fatigues with crying; intermittent stertor clearly audible; no persistent stridor when held upright.

exam.q: Positional observation (supine vs prone vs upright)
exam.a: Marked suprasternal and subcostal retraction when supine with SpO₂ falling to 90–91%; immediate improvement in saturation with appropriate positioning under supervision (critical positional finding).
Marked micrognathia with retrognathic mandible relative to the midface.
Evident glossoptosis with posterior tongue displacement causing airway obstruction, particularly when supine.
Associated U-shaped cleft palate; no cleft lip.
Weight loss of approximately 9–10% from birth weight; mildly dry mucous membranes.
Good bilateral air entry; no focal crackles.
No significant murmur; good peripheral perfusion.
No overt limb anomaly on initial examination; syndromic associations (e.g. Stickler syndrome) should be considered in context.

problemList: Micrognathia, glossoptosis and cleft palate consistent with Pierre Robin sequence
Positional upper-airway obstruction with supine desaturation, improving with positioning
Feeding failure with approximately 9–10% weight loss from birth weight
Incomplete screening for associated syndromic conditions
Family distress requiring a safe interim airway and feeding plan pending multidisciplinary evaluation
G1C6.problemRepresentation: A 6-day-old male neonate with micrognathia, glossoptosis and cleft palate consistent with Pierre Robin sequence, with positional upper-airway obstruction confirmed by supine desaturation that improves with positioning, complicated by feeding failure and 9–10% weight loss from birth weight, representing a neonatal airway emergency that requires urgent assessment of airway, hydration and feeding safety, in contrast to isolated cleft palate without airway compromise.

exam.a: Well-appearing, cheerful child; developmental milestones age-appropriate on observation.

exam.q: Measurement and morphology of the facial lesion
exam.a: Well-demarcated dark brown to black pigmented plaque approximately 6 cm in diameter involving the left cheek and temple, with mildly thickened leathery texture and coarse terminal hair; no ulceration or bleeding.

exam.q: Detailed assessment of color and surface
exam.a: Homogeneous pigmentation throughout; no nodules, focal darkening or regression/depigmentation.
Three to four smaller satellite melanocytic nevi on the trunk and back with similar morphology.

exam.q: Head and neck lymph node examination
exam.a: No lymphadenopathy.

exam.q: Examination of the eyes and eyelids
exam.a: Lesion does not involve the eyelid margin or impair vision; no ocular melanosis.
No involvement of the oral commissure, eyelid closure or facial movement.
Normal; no focal neurological deficit; head circumference appropriate for age.

problemList: Large congenital melanocytic nevus of the left face, present since birth with proportional growth
Multiple satellite nevi on the trunk and back, conferring increased risk of neurocutaneous melanosis requiring further evaluation
No current features of malignant transformation (no ulceration, new nodularity, atypical pigment change or disproportionate growth)
Emerging psychosocial impact from peer attention to the facial lesion
No established surveillance or specialist referral plan for long-term care
G1C7.problemRepresentation: A 3-year-old girl with a large congenital melanocytic nevus of the left face present since birth with proportional growth and multiple truncal satellite nevi conferring increased risk of neurocutaneous melanosis, without current features of malignant transformation but with emerging psychosocial impact, requiring referral to pediatric dermatology/plastic surgery for risk-stratified screening and long-term physical and psychosocial management planning.
